examples.scenario: A 2022 composite DTM pixel is used even though a native time-stamped DTM exists for the same parcel.
examples.reason: Composite cells can be bilinearly resampled and mix survey lineage; prefer the native time-stamped source.

examples.scenario: The pipeline labels every EA LiDAR parcel result as ±15 cm accurate.
examples.reason: ±15 cm RMSE is a programme requirement, not a measured parcel-specific error.

examples.scenario: A ground-truth survey from another project and year is used to claim target-survey accuracy.
examples.reason: Ground truth must be linked to the actual target survey and valid reuse period.

examples.scenario: The parcel is under woodland and DSM nominal point density is treated as DTM ground density.
examples.reason: EA explicitly warns that DTM ground density under vegetation can be lower.

examples.scenario: A DSM maximum over a building is reported as bare-earth parcel maximum.
examples.reason: DSM includes objects; terrain extrema require DTM lineage.

examples.scenario: An index catalogue shows no target survey but a nearby tile is substituted.
examples.reason: AOI coverage must match the target parcel and product.

examples.scenario: Survey metadata says an older geoid model, but processing silently assumes OSGM15.
examples.reason: Transformation/geoid model must follow survey-period metadata or be explicitly reconciled.

examples.scenario: OSTN02/OSGM02 heights are directly compared with OSTN15/OSGM15 heights.
examples.reason: Legacy and current model outputs can differ materially and require a documented conversion path.

examples.scenario: The OSGM15 0.008 m GB standard error is added as if it were total LiDAR error.
examples.reason: OSGM15 model error excludes GNSS, LiDAR, checkpoint and other components.

examples.scenario: OS Net station height standard error is treated as the target raster vertical RMSE.
examples.reason: Control-network precision and raster survey accuracy are distinct components.

examples.scenario: The Lite OSTN15/OSGM15 developer grid is used for a precision terminal result.
examples.reason: OS documents the Lite pack as lower accuracy than the full model.

examples.scenario: A coordinate labelled WGS84 is assumed to be precise ETRS89 without realization metadata.
examples.reason: High-accuracy GB transformation requires explicit reference-frame provenance.

examples.scenario: A National Grid coordinate is parsed as degrees because units were not recorded.
examples.reason: OS National Grid eastings/northings are metres and require explicit format/unit handling.

examples.scenario: A 1 m composite cell created by bilinear resampling becomes the terminal minimum.
examples.reason: Resampled composite values are derived and need lineage/uncertainty treatment.

examples.scenario: A survey passes RMSE but its relative/random error is not checked.
examples.reason: EA publishes both absolute and relative/random error expectations.

examples.scenario: A ground-truth point accuracy of ±3 cm is treated as zero uncertainty.
examples.reason: Ground-truth/checkpoint survey error must remain a distinct uncertainty component.

examples.scenario: Two runs use the same DTM tile but different transformation model versions and matching rounded heights.
examples.reason: Reproducibility requires identical datum/model provenance, not just rounded outputs.

examples.scenario: Composite DTM survey epoch is ignored although the parcel has changed terrain between surveys.
examples.reason: Survey date/epoch is part of target lineage and can matter for real terrain change.

examples.scenario: A target parcel has sparse ground support but interpolation is accepted without a support ledger.
examples.reason: Sparse support and any derived fill must be visible in uncertainty and replay evidence.

examples.scenario: The final height difference is published before canonical point, boundary, target survey and error-budget evidence exist.
examples.reason: Terminal numeric output remains blocked until canonical inputs and executable QC are present.
